aiExplanation: This function decodes a ciphertext that was encoded in a rail-fence pattern. It calculates the increment (`inc`) between characters in the same diagonal by dividing the total length by the number of rows. It then iterates through each column, reading characters at positions spaced by `inc + 1` apart, which follows the diagonal pattern. When a position exceeds the string length, it moves to the next diagonal line by incrementing `line` and adjusting `pos`. Finally, it trims whitespace and returns the decoded message.

aiExplanation: This function uses the same rail-fence decoding algorithm as the first solution, but instead of using `trim()`, it uses `trimEnd()` to remove only trailing whitespace. It calculates the column increment (`inc`), iterates through diagonals by reading characters spaced `inc + 1` positions apart, and handles line transitions when positions exceed the string length. This version preserves leading whitespace while removing trailing spaces, which is important for correct decoding of the ciphertext.

aiExplanation: This solution takes an alternative approach by first constructing a 2D matrix from the encoded text, where each row contains `n` characters (total length divided by number of rows). It then decodes by reading diagonally: starting from each column position, it reads characters while moving down and to the right across the matrix. This diagonal reading pattern reverses the rail-fence encoding and reconstructs the original message. Finally, it returns the result after trimming trailing whitespace with `trimEnd()`.
